headline: Dollar flat into midterms; PBOC reins in yuan, dovish RBA hike hits Aussie, TWD slumps
summary: The dollar index edged up about 0.07% to near 101.83 in a choppy session, as a jump in US job openings to 7.52 million offset caution before the midterms and swings in oil on mixed Iran headlines. The peso, won and franc held up, while the Aussie, yen and Taiwan dollar fell about 0.5% and the yuan about 0.35% on a dovish RBA hike, the PBOC's reserve move and record foreign selling of Taiwan stocks.
drivers: The PBOC will raise the FX reserve ratio to 6% from 4% on Nov 15, draining about $24bn, and USD/CNH jumped 0.35% to 6.67. The RBA hiked to 4.85% but on a 6–3 vote and dropped its tightening bias, sending the Aussie to a two-week low near 0.6961.
AI selloff drains Asian equity money

The Taiex and Kospi both fell 3.6%; foreigners sold about NT$107bn of Taiwan and 1.5tn won of Korean shares. The Taiwan dollar hit a 1.5-year closing low of 32.760, and the ringgit eased to about 4.0755, even as the Nasdaq rebounded 0.8% in New York.
Strong US data lifts yields, yen slides
JOLTS openings rose to 7.52 million vs 7.10 million expected and long-dated Treasury yields rose up to 7bp. With Japan on holiday, USD/JPY rose about 0.5% to 158.68 despite Tokyo's warnings.
view: Neutral to mildly bearish for the next 1–2 weeks: cheaper oil and a divided Fed cap the dollar against Europe, but in Asia the PBOC is now slowing the yuan and AI-driven equity outflows are hitting the Taiwan dollar and ringgit, so dollar dips there stay shallow. I fade the dollar against the yen near Tokyo's 159–160 line and against the ringgit into Bank Negara, but back it against the Taiwan dollar while foreigners keep selling. A DXY close above 102.50 after the midterms or payrolls would make me neutral; a close below 101.40 confirms the downtrend.
ideas: Long 32.65–32.75 as record foreign selling of Taiwan stocks overwhelms the central bank's smoothing; for 33.00, stop 32.50.
Re-sell 159.20–159.50 into Tokyo's intervention zone with a December BoJ hike still live; for 157.00, stop 160.30.
Hold the 4.055–4.065 sale into Bank Negara's Nov 5 decision; for 4.010, stop 4.085.
review: USD/JPY's short and AUD/USD's long were stopped at 158.60 and 0.6970 as the yen slid and a dovish RBA hike hit the Aussie, and the USD/CNH sale, about 0.2% against, is closed after the PBOC's reserve move. USD/CAD's short is about 0.2% in favour, USD/IDR's long about 0.25% in favour and the ringgit sale about 0.35% against; USD/TWD broke its 32.75 range top and turns to a long.

eurusd.note: Flat at about 1.1188, holding last week's gains as the dollar chopped around before the midterms.
eurusd.why: Neither side moved much. The dollar dipped early on midterm caution and mixed Iran headlines, then recovered after US job openings jumped to 7.52 million against 7.10 million expected. Euro-area news was light, and a rise of up to 7bp in long-dated US yields kept the euro from building on Monday's one-month high near 1.1237.
eurusd.outlook: I keep the 1.1130–1.1250 range: cheaper oil helps Europe, but strong US labour data and French fiscal worries cap rallies. A close above 1.1250 would open 1.1300.
eurusd.watch: US midterm results (Nov 4), euro-area flash CPI, US payrolls (Nov 6), oil and Iran talks.

view.call: 1.1130–1.1250; oil relief vs strong US data, France.

gbpusd.note: Little changed near 1.3409 after a Reuters-quoted 0.1% gain, still just under the 1.3450 range top.
gbpusd.why: Sterling barely moved. A 1.1% drop in the FTSE weighed on risk appetite, but expectations of a Bank of England hike on Thursday, backed by strong factory surveys, kept rate support in place. The dollar's own chop around the JOLTS beat and midterm caution set the tone.
gbpusd.outlook: I keep the 1.3280–1.3450 range and buy dips: a hawkish BoE hike should hold the floor, but I need a close above 1.3450 to chase it higher.
gbpusd.watch: BoE decision and guidance (Nov 5), UK gilts, US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: 1.3280–1.3450; buy dips, BoE Nov 5 is the swing.

audusd.note: Down about 0.5% to 0.6964 after a two-week low near 0.6961; a dovish RBA hike stopped the long.
audusd.why: The Aussie did the moving. The RBA raised its cash rate 25bp to 4.85%, an 18-year high, but the 6–3 vote, the dropped line about further hikes and sharply weaker growth forecasts read as dovish. Bullock said it was probably best to pause and assess, and markets cut the odds of a 5.10% peak to about 30%. Iron ore near $90 added to the pressure.
audusd.outlook: My long was stopped below 0.6970; I move to a 0.6930–0.7050 range. Heavy short positioning and the best carry in G10 should limit losses, but the 200-day near 0.7050–0.7080 caps rallies.
audusd.watch: China trade data, US payrolls (Nov 6), iron ore, AI-stock sentiment.

view.call: 0.6930–0.7050; dovish RBA vs carry, short positioning.

usdjpy.note: Up about 0.5% to 158.68, the yen's weakest close in weeks; the short was stopped above 158.60.
usdjpy.why: The yen did the moving. With Japan on holiday, the rate gap of about 275bp between the Fed and the BoJ took over: strong US job openings and a 7bp rise in long-dated Treasury yields lifted the pair through 158.30. Finance Minister Katayama's repeated warnings that Tokyo will act on disorderly moves did little to slow it.
usdjpy.outlook: I was stopped, but the cap is still there: I re-sell closer to Tokyo's line at 159.20–159.50 for 157.00, since every push toward 159–160 has drawn warnings or intervention this year. A close above 160.30 would end the call.
usdjpy.watch: Tokyo intervention talk, Japan wage data, US midterm results (Nov 4) and payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: Re-sell 159.20–159.50; Tokyo's 160 line, BoJ Dec live.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.3% to 0.8209 after a seven-week low at 0.8149; the range floor held.
usdchf.why: Swiss inflation jumped to 1.5% in October, above every forecast and the highest in almost three years, which pushed the franc to a seven-week high against the dollar and a five-month high against the euro. But core inflation held at 0.5%, so the SNB's case to act is weak, and the dollar's recovery after the JOLTS beat pulled the pair back into its range.
usdchf.outlook: I keep the 0.8150–0.8280 range: the floor held on the first test, and crowded franc longs plus possible SNB selling should slow further gains. A daily close below 0.8150 would open 0.8050.
usdchf.watch: Weekly sight deposits (Nov 9), SNB speakers, US payrolls (Nov 6).

usdcad.note: Up about 0.2% to 1.4010 after an early low near 1.3950; the short is still in favour.
usdcad.why: Oil set the pace. Crude bounced early after a reported US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, lifting the loonie toward 1.3950, then fell back on unconfirmed reports of concessions in US-Iran talks. Governor Macklem told parliament further hikes may be needed, but the stronger US dollar after the JOLTS beat pulled the pair back above 1.40.
usdcad.outlook: I keep the short for 1.3850: the BoC's hawkish tone and trade-deal hopes still outweigh choppy oil. A close above 1.4040 would end the call, and Friday's jobs data is the risk.
usdcad.watch: Canada jobs and US payrolls (Nov 6), oil and Iran talks, BoC speakers.

view.call: Short from 1.4030–1.4050; hawkish BoC, trade hopes.

usdcnh.note: Up about 0.35% to 6.67, the dollar's biggest daily gain against the yuan since May.
usdcnh.why: Beijing did the moving. The PBOC said it will raise the FX reserve requirement ratio to 6% from 4% from Nov 15, its first increase in nearly five years, draining about $24bn of dollar liquidity to slow the yuan's rally. It reversed a 2023 cut and was read as a clear signal against one-way bets after the onshore yuan hit 6.64 on Monday.
usdcnh.outlook: I close the sale, about 0.2% against, because the central bank is now openly leaning against the yuan's gains. I move to a 6.62–6.70 range until the fixings show how far Beijing wants to slow it.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, FX RRR effective Nov 15, China trade data.

view.call: 6.62–6.70; PBOC now slowing the yuan's rise.

usdhkd.note: Little changed near 7.846, still close to the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved the pair. A wide gap between US and Hong Kong rates keeps carry traders selling Hong Kong dollars, which holds the pair near 7.85, where the HKMA would buy them to defend the peg. The yuan's drop on the PBOC move had little effect.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: the carry gap pins it near 7.85, and only a sharp rise in HIBOR or HKMA buying would pull it lower.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA operations at 7.85, HIBOR, US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Up about 0.3% to near 1.2813, near the top of its range as Asian currencies slid.
usdsgd.why: Regional flows did the moving. The yuan fell on the PBOC's reserve move and the Taiwan dollar hit a 1.5-year low on record foreign stock selling, dragging the Singapore dollar lower with them. It stayed firm in trade-weighted terms, rising against the ringgit, as the MAS keeps the S$NEER on a strong path.
usdsgd.outlook: I widen the range to 1.2740–1.2860: regional outflows lift the top, while a strong S$NEER limits Singapore dollar weakness. A close above 1.2860 would mean broader Asian stress.
usdsgd.watch: US midterm results (Nov 4), China trade data, US payrolls (Nov 6).

usdkrw.note: Won firmed 2.8 to 1,341.0 at the Seoul close, despite a 3.6% Kospi slide.
usdkrw.why: The won held up better than its stocks. The Kospi fell 3.6% on AI-spending worries and foreigners sold about 1.5tn won of shares, yet the pair opened at 1,346 and drifted lower as the dollar softened in Asian hours and exporters sold dollars. The won is near the strong end of its yearly range, which draws profit-taking on dips.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep the 1,330–1,355 range: heavy foreign selling limits won gains, but exporters and a soft dollar against Europe cap the upside. A close above 1,355 would point to 1,370.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows, US midterm results (Nov 4), US payrolls (Nov 6).

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar fell 16.8 cents to 32.760, a 1.5-year closing low, after touching 32.86.
usdtwd.why: Equity outflows did the moving. The Taiex plunged 3.6%, its seventh-biggest point drop on record, and foreigners sold about NT$107bn of shares, taking four-day selling to about NT$362bn. Exporters sold dollars in the morning after the central bank lifted their daily selling cap, but they stepped back after noon and turnover hit a near-record $5.3bn.
usdtwd.outlook: The range top broke, so I turn long: record outflows are overwhelming the central bank's smoothing, which officials say has no fixed line. I buy dips to 32.65–32.75 for 33.00; a close below 32.50 would end the call.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, US midterm results (Nov 4), TSMC October sales (Nov 10).

view.call: Long 32.65–32.75; record foreign selling of Taiex.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit eased to 4.0735/0775 at the 6pm close from 4.0695/0735 as AI trades unwound.
usdmyr.why: The ringgit slipped on its own side. Malaysia has been a big winner of the AI investment boom through chips, so the unwinding of AI trades across Asia hit it even as the dollar was flat against Europe. It opened slightly firmer on US-Iran diplomacy hopes but faded with regional currencies.
usdmyr.outlook: I hold the sale for 4.010, now about 0.35% against: a Bank Negara move to start normalising rates on Nov 5 should restore the ringgit's lead. A close above 4.085 would end the call.
usdmyr.watch: Bank Negara decision (Nov 5), US payrolls (Nov 6), oil, regional chip stocks.

usdphp.note: Peso rose 27 centavos to 63.47, its strongest close since Oct 21, after the holiday.
usdphp.why: The peso did the moving. Monday's near 8% oil slump cut the Philippines' import bill, and remittances after the long weekend added dollar supply. Governor Remolona said the BSP steps in when depreciation runs too fast because it feeds inflation, and President Marcos's recent reassurances helped sentiment.
usdphp.outlook: I lower the range to 63.30–64.20: cheaper oil and BSP resolve support the peso, but weak growth and outflows keep the 64.17 record low in view. A close below 63.30 would open 63.00.
usdphp.watch: Philippine October CPI (Nov 5), BSP comments, oil, US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: 63.30–64.20; oil relief, BSP smooths both ways.

usdidr.note: Rupiah eased 4 points to 18,160 (Bloomberg); the JISDOR rate firmed to 18,148.
usdidr.why: The rupiah slipped on its own side. Foreign money kept leaving Indonesian assets, and Bank Indonesia's Destry Damayanti named the Middle East conflict, tight US policy and weak sentiment toward emerging markets as the pressures. A better-than-expected trade surplus helped it firm early.
usdidr.outlook: I keep the long for 18,300, about 0.25% in favour, on outflows and policy uncertainty. A close below 18,060 would end the call.
usdidr.watch: Indonesia Q3 GDP (Nov 5), Bank Indonesia operations, foreign bond flows.

usdinr.note: Rupee firmed to about 94.73 per dollar from 94.89, helped by lower oil.
usdinr.why: The rupee edged up as Brent held near four-week lows after Monday's slide, which eases India's import bill. Gains were small because the RBI is expected to buy dollars near 94.50 to rebuild reserves after building a large short forward book.
usdinr.outlook: I keep the 94.50–95.50 range: the RBI caps both sides and oil sets the drift. A sustained Brent drop below $100 would open 94.20.
usdinr.watch: Oil and Iran talks, RBI dollar buying, US midterm results (Nov 4).

view.call: 94.50–95.50; RBI caps both ways, oil sets drift.

eurjpy.note: Up about 0.5% to near 177.5, close to the top of its range, as the yen slid.
eurjpy.why: The yen did all the moving. The euro was flat against the dollar, but the yen fell about 0.5% on the wide rate gap and higher US yields during Japan's holiday. Tokyo's warnings have not stopped the drift, which leaves the cross near 177.8, the range high.
eurjpy.outlook: I keep the 175.5–177.8 range and favour selling near the top, as Tokyo's warnings intensify near 159–160 in USD/JPY. A close above 177.8 would open 179.
eurjpy.watch: Tokyo intervention talk, Japan wage data, euro-area flash CPI.

cnhjpy.note: Up about 0.1% to near 23.79 as the yen's slide outpaced the yuan's.
cnhjpy.why: The two legs pulled against each other. The yuan had its biggest one-day drop since May after the PBOC raised the FX reserve ratio, while the yen fell slightly more on the rate gap. That left the cross near the top of its range.
cnhjpy.outlook: I widen the range a little to 23.3–23.9: Beijing is now slowing the yuan and Tokyo is guarding the yen, so neither leg has room to run.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, FX RRR effective Nov 15, Tokyo intervention talk.

watch: Next: US midterm results (Nov 4), the BoE, Bank Negara, Philippine CPI and Indonesia GDP (Nov 5), US payrolls and Canada jobs (Nov 6), the PBOC's FX reserve hike (Nov 15), plus Tokyo's 159–160 line and foreign selling of Asian tech stocks.
sources: Reuters via Yahoo Finance (PBOC FX reserve ratio)
